title: WSJ (via TechCrunch, 21:48Z Nov 17): the SEC is opening a civil probe into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors; neither the SEC nor Nvidia has commented; scope unknown; Commerce has investigated Megaspeed since late 2024 over suspected diversion of Nvidia chips to China
body:
# WSJ: SEC opening a civil probe of Nvidia's disclosures (Nov 17)

**Read at TechCrunch (posted 1:48 PM PST Nov 17 = 21:48Z, Rebecca Bellan, 'In Brief'):** "The Securities and Exchange Commission is opening a civil probe into Nvidia over whether the company's disclosures misled investors", "according to The Wall Street Journal." TechCrunch gives no further scope and carries no SEC or Nvidia comment. **WALTER did not read the WSJ article**; its sourcing (named or unnamed) is not visible.

**Context in the same report (TechCrunch, no source given):** "The Commerce Department has been investigating Megaspeed since late 2024 under suspicion that the company diverted some of its Nvidia chips to China, which would violate U.S. export laws." A search summary (00:5xZ) adds, attributed to the WSJ, that the Justice Department leads several investigations involving a Megaspeed executive, and that Nvidia dropped its Singapore sales breakdown from its disclosures last year. Those two points are search-summary only; WALTER did not verify them. Personal allegations about named individuals in some reports are not carried.

**Why it matters:** this is a regulatory probe of the issuer's disclosures, not a reported event inside the results. It follows the 11/12 CEO transition (Kress interim), Bessent's 10-day demand (card 20261116-002), the results (019, 020) and tonight's titles that Nvidia is not reinstating Huang (023). Nvidia previously paid a $5.5 million SEC penalty (May 2022, cryptomining disclosures; search summary). NVDA closed 155.46 on Nov 17 (vendor), after hours 158.56 at 21:47Z, BEFORE the 21:48Z TechCrunch post; the after-hours reaction to the probe is not observed. TechCrunch's 'more than 10% since Huang departed' has no time basis.

**Ask:** VULCAN grades it (SEC, EDGAR 8-K or company statement). Source: Polymarket relay on Will's X bookmarks (21:04Z), checked to TechCrunch.

title: Equinor confirms an ongoing cyber-attack on certain IT systems (company release 18:55 CET Nov 17): operations and production not affected, no indication data was stolen, authorities being informed
body:
# Equinor detected an ongoing cyber-attack (company release, Nov 17 18:55 CET)

**Read at equinor.com** (release 17 November 2026 18:55 CET = 17:55Z, last modified 19:40 CET): "Equinor has detected an ongoing cyber-attack against certain IT systems." "Relevant resources have been mobilised to neutralise the attack and regain full integrity." "There are no indications that data has been stolen." "The attack has not affected Equinor's operations and production." "Relevant authorities are being informed." "Equinor will provide updates when new information is available."

No actor, method or system named. Secondary: Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) is in contact with Equinor and offered help (search summary, not read). Equinor is Europe's largest gas supplier: the relevance is to European gas supply confidence (TTF, HANS-T-07 ladder; named TTFZ26 vendor 85.48 Nov 17, not a settle), not to any reported flow loss.

**Not the bank-supplier class** (no bank, core vendor or payment system), so PRIORITY, not IMMEDIATE. Source: two X bookmarks (@WatcherGuru 19:12Z, @LeadingReport 20:34Z), checked to the company's own release.
